lane_method: Holdout = hide-and-recover: whole fault segments withheld with a 1.5 km collar; catalogue-based features derived only from visible faults; visible faults masked pixel-exactly; pooled DTI (alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel) with cluster-bootstrap 95% CI.
hypothesis: H2: geothermal-vent conduit propensity. Blind faults that host hydrothermal conduits are missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue (the private test labels are expert-labeled NEW faults), so a field keyed to strain + seismicity + magnetic curvature + basement depth + weak catalogue proximity, reinforced by GDR #1391 2 m temperature probes and paleo-geothermal vents, should recover catalogue-hidden faults that catalogue-dotted fields cannot.
mechanism: Soft-probability dotted emission on the exact competition grid (EPSG:32611, 3730x3292, 100 m, origin 243350/4508550). Propensity = 0.35 catalogue proximity + 0.20 geodetic dilatation + 0.13 shear + 0.13 seismicity + 0.10 magnetic tilt/curvature + 0.05 depth-to-basement + 0.02 2 m temperature + 0.02 paleo-vent, robust-percentile normalised, lightly Gaussian-smoothed, 44,090 NMS-separated (>=3 px) maxima emitted as soft probabilities, 0.0 on catalogue faults and outside the footprint. DTI(alpha=0.2,beta=0.8): TP_w rewards dots near withheld faults; FN_w heavily penalises missed faults; FP_w is cheap for isolated dots because the triangular kernel truncates at 300 m.
named_non_fault_mimic: Geothermal surface expressions not fault-controlled (fumaroles/springs on lithologic contacts), paleo-playa/sinter deposits, non-tectonic seismic swarms, cultural noise (roads, claims). Mitigation: thermal/vent layers down-weighted to 0.02 each and gated to require strain/curvature concurrence; catalogue proximity limited to 0.35 so emission is not a copy of the mapped traces.
